synopsis: GRVA-18-55 is a January 2024 UNECE informal document submitted by the United Kingdom, arguing that the proposal to add virtual testing to UN Regulation No. 152 for AEB did not address all aspects of credible virtual-testing capability [f1279, f7689]. Its specific concern was that the proposal appeared to require physical testing only for the final toolchain, whereas physical testing should be used and evidenced for every component [f7690]. The planning chapter describes the document as validating the toolchain against physical tests and then using it within the assessed envelope [f9746]. These accounts distinguish a general validation approach from the unresolved question of whether its component-level evidence is sufficient; the corpus also reports a November 2025 Russian Federation call for mandatory physical verification of the virtual model [f7690, f9746, f8187].

relations.note: Both report the January 2024 document's criticism of incomplete virtual-testing credibility provisions.
Identifies missing component-level physical evidence behind the broader credibility criticism.
Specifies the United Kingdom's objection to final-toolchain-only physical testing.
Restates the component-evidence demand and adds Russia's later physical-verification position.
Clarifies that physical validation should cover every component, not merely the final toolchain.
Places the United Kingdom's credibility criticism alongside a later Russian verification demand.
